channel.title: Diffbrief · Inference
channel.description: Daily inference stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: ggml 1.0 adds FP8, YaRN controls and backend inference optimizations
item.description: The release adds FP8 support and configurable YaRN truncation alongside backend work including quantized matmuls, MoE fusion and a Vulkan prefill FlashAttention path. These changes matter to engineers running models across varied hardware.

item.title: DeepSeek Ultrafast reports 85,000-token/s prefill on eight B300 GPUs
item.description: The engine reports processing a million-token prefill in 11.7 seconds on eight B300s and supports shared KV cache across servers; the page also gives reproduction instructions. These measurements and implementation details are useful to engineers evaluating long-context inference setups.

item.title: vLLM serves a 753B-parameter GLM model across two DGX Stations
item.description: The setup uses TP=2 over RDMA to serve a model requiring about 464 GB of GPU memory, with FP8 KV-cache storage and prefix caching; throughput peaks at 607.8 tokens per second at concurrency 16. It provides a measured reference for multi-node model serving and its latency trade-offs.

item.title: G-STAR scales token groups with spatial compression for up to 64× compression
item.description: G-STAR co-scales spatial compression and product-quantization group size, reporting strong results at 32× and effective 64× compression across five image-generation benchmarks. Its semi-autoregressive decoder addresses the added dependencies, making the work relevant to generation quality and latency trade-offs.

item.title: llama.cpp 1.0.0 formalizes a portable foundation for local model inference
item.description: The release establishes a stable API for a portable C/C++ runtime that supports multimodal models across hardware, using quantization and optimized backends. That foundation matters to teams deploying local, cross-platform inference.

item.title: NVIDIA exposes Jetson DLA inference to Python through cuDLA
item.description: The Python API supports hybrid workflows that coordinate DLA inference with GPU preprocessing and postprocessing on CUDA streams, and the excerpt walks through the inference lifecycle. This is useful for engineers balancing inference power efficiency and GPU capacity on supported hardware.

item.title: A project runs 16B models on devices with about 1 GB of RAM
item.description: The project streams weights from flash and uses custom kernels to run 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on a TV box and an old iPad; reported speeds were measured on-device. Its memory and kernel techniques are relevant to constrained inference deployments.

item.title: Edge0 open-sources 145B and 120B models for local inference
item.description: Edge0 says its 145B model runs on a compatible laptop with peak memory of 29GB and decoding above 80 tokens per second, alongside an inference framework and deployment tools. The release makes concrete claims about running large models locally, though the excerpt doesn't provide benchmark methodology.

item.title: PISA-E adapts LLM ensemble size and composition to prompt cost and quality
item.description: PISA-E predicts model capabilities and selects ensemble membership and size under an adjustable cost-quality preference; it achieves the highest macro-average task performance among evaluated ensemble routers. This is a practical approach to serving heterogeneous requests at different cost targets.

item.title: SGLang-Neuron brings SGLang serving and RL rollouts to AWS Trainium
item.description: The out-of-tree plugin connects SGLang to Trainium while retaining SGLang’s server interface and generation APIs; it runs on native PyTorch. This gives serving teams a familiar integration path, though the excerpt includes no performance or cost results.

item.title: Bedrock cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort and maxTokens affect cost
item.description: The guide tests four request-level settings and shows how to verify their effects using response metadata, logs and billing data. This gives serving teams a way to measure cost controls without changing the model or prompt.

item.title: AWS Budgets can cap Bedrock spend by IAM principal without application code
item.description: Bedrock’s principal attribution, CUR or Cost Explorer, and AWS Budgets budget actions provide per-identity cost reporting and enforceable limits using AWS-native features. This offers a simpler baseline before building custom spend enforcement.

item.title: APEX removes a separate fake-score network from few-step video generation
item.description: APEX uses condition shifting to estimate the generated distribution's velocity with the generator's own parameters, avoiding an independent fake-score network. It reports higher instruction fulfillment and visual-aesthetics scores than S2-Avatar, with 30% net human preference for instruction following.

item.title: Huawei's MACaQ quantizes a 122B model in 64 minutes using 32.5 GB
item.description: MACaQ supports quantization across text, image, video, and audio models; its excerpt claims a 122B-parameter model can be quantized in 64 minutes with 32.5 GB of device memory. The reported speed and quality comparisons make it worth evaluating for local inference and serving.

item.title: MACaQ quantizes weights and activations with layer-local MXFP4 transforms
item.description: MACaQ applies per-layer activation transforms and Hessian-aware code refinement for W4A4 quantization; it adds 2.3% overhead over pure MXFP4 on Qwen3-32B in vLLM and matches a Llama-3-8B comparison's best perplexity in 11 times less quantization time. The streaming, layer-at-a-time design targets both memory use and practical quantization cost.

item.title: Meta targets ad-ranking compute where each unit has greater impact
item.description: Meta says the value of extra compute varies by ad request, model and chip as ranking models grow toward LLM scale. The excerpt omits the allocation method and results, but the problem is directly relevant to serving under constrained compute.

item.title: SageMaker bidirectional streaming adds usage metering for model providers
item.description: The feature lets Marketplace model providers report actual consumption for streaming inference while endpoint infrastructure charges remain separate; Deepgram is the launch partner for STT and TTS billing. It addresses the economics of charging for long-lived real-time inference streams.

item.title: ExecuTorch WebGPU runs PyTorch models in browsers, up to 10× faster on decode
item.description: ExecuTorch’s WebGPU backend runs exported .pte models in-browser across LLM, vision, and speech workloads, with 4–7× faster prefill and 2–10× faster decode than its CPU path on the same machine. It offers a practical route to private, offline-capable GPU inference without converting frameworks.

item.title: Alpamayo 2 Edge reaches 160–190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency on DRIVE AGX Thor
item.description: The 2B-parameter vision-language-action model uses conditional reasoning and a diffusion action expert; closed-loop RL improved driving performance 48.9% over the best checkpoint without it. The deployment recipes and latency figures offer practical guidance for constrained, real-time inference.

item.title: NVIDIA Snapshot restores GPU inference replicas up to 36× faster than cold starts
item.description: The Kubernetes checkpoint-and-restore system captures CPU and GPU memory, bringing tested replicas online in 3.6–42.7 seconds versus cold starts taking minutes. The measurements show how preserving initialized GPU state can reduce serving startup time.

item.title: Google adds confidential-inference TPU 8tx and long-context TPU 8i Max
item.description: Google says TPU 8tx provides hardware-level security for sensitive inference, while TPU 8i Max is designed for massive context windows. These workload-specific accelerator designs are relevant to serving agent systems, though the excerpt gives no performance figures.

item.title: DeepX targets 20B–100B models at 10–30 tokens per second under 5 W
item.description: DeepX says its taped-out DX-M2 uses Samsung processor-in-memory technology to target models with 20 billion to 100 billion parameters at 10–30 tokens per second under 5 W. These are projected capabilities, not reported measurements, but they point to the power constraints of edge inference.

item.title: Inference engineering guide introduces model-GPU interaction and production tools
item.description: The guide is aimed at platform engineers and covers how models and GPUs work together, running inference in production and tools used in the field. It offers a starting point for engineers entering inference, though the excerpt gives no specific techniques or measurements.

item.title: HOPE prunes MoE experts to reduce inference-time memory
item.description: The piece identifies expert weights as a major MoE memory cost: in the cited Qwen3.5-122B example, they account for about 95% of the roughly 250 GB footprint, though only 8 of 256 experts are used per token. Pruning could reduce memory without dynamic expert loading or retraining.

item.title: NaiveAI pitches a 2,100-token/s coding model built on MiMo-V2.5
item.description: Naive-N0.5-Flash continues training from Xiaomi’s sparse Mixture-of-Experts model and pairs it with NaiveAI’s NaiveRT inference engine. The review’s focus on coding ability alongside generation speed is relevant when evaluating fast-serving models for engineering work.

item.title: H100 SXM rental prices range from $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour
item.description: The comparison finds a 4.57× spread for H100 SXM 80GB rentals, from RunPod Community to Azure, and separates GPU variants to avoid misleading comparisons. The price gap matters for inference capacity planning and GPU procurement.

item.title: Flide claims up to 9.5× faster decision-model inference with exact state forking
item.description: Flide says exact state forking makes Jev-style decision models up to 9.5× faster than vLLM and SGLang; its demo tags 10,000 emails with eight questions each in 28 seconds on one H200. The technique and workload figures are worth examining for specialized inference serving.

item.title: Inference from Scratch builds an LLM engine from weights to paged attention
item.description: The series builds a C++ and CUDA inference engine, covering transformer operations, KV caching, batching and paged attention, alongside extensive notes. It gives engineers a hands-on path through the mechanics behind serving and optimizing models.

item.title: TPU Sync moves KV caches and model weights across a co-designed memory hierarchy
item.description: The open-source C++ library uses asynchronous DMA to move TPU-tiled tensors across HBM, host DRAM, storage, and the data-center network while computation continues. Its approach to reducing transfer bottlenecks matters for disaggregated inference and reinforcement-learning rollouts.

item.title: AutoCompress searches model pruning against measured serving constraints
item.description: AutoCompress uses serving-engine cost models to find heterogeneous pruning structures, improving average accuracy over Minitron across RTX 5070, RTX 5080 and H100. Hardware-aware compression can better match real latency, throughput and memory limits than parameter counts.

item.title: A 16 GiB memory budget runs 120B MoE models on an M1 Max
item.description: A prototype keeps most MoE weights on SSD and runs gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B under a 16 GiB process-memory budget on an M1 Max. The comparison with TUFF and the explicit memory constraint make this relevant to local inference trade-offs.

item.title: Underdog Woof runs CPU-only TTS from a 40.6 MB model file
item.description: The two-voice English TTS model is 40.6 MB, uses 402 MB peak memory for Juno, and runs at 13.8× real time on one Apple M5 Max CPU thread; Mira reports 1.42% word error on the stated hard-case set. Its small footprint and CPU throughput are useful reference points for edge inference.

item.title: Google expands its TPU lineup with 8tx and 8i Max systems
item.description: The announcement positions 8tx for large-scale training and 8i Max for large context windows and high compute density per rack; earlier 8t and 8i models are reported to improve training performance by up to 2.7x and inference price performance by 80%. AI infrastructure teams get new accelerator options, though the excerpt offers vendor-reported comparisons.

item.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL brings million-token context and speculative decoding to JumpStart
item.description: Super VL pairs a 120B-parameter MoE backbone with 12B active parameters, supports up to 1 million tokens, and includes a multi-token prediction head for speculative decoding. JumpStart offers NVFP4 and BF16 variants, giving serving teams concrete deployment and precision options.

item.title: Next-Concept Modeling generates text with coarse-to-fine parallel steps
item.description: The method encodes text into hierarchical discrete codes, then predicts all codes at each level in parallel; the abstract reports better generative perplexity than diffusion models at matched parameter scales. Parallel generation could affect inference throughput and quality trade-offs.

item.title: A CPU-only runtime fits a 284B-parameter model in 64 GB of RAM
item.description: The project reports running a 284B-parameter DeepSeek model at 1.71 bits per weight in 64 GB of RAM without a GPU, with 9.1–14.7 tokens/s decode. These measurements make a striking case for CPU-first inference at low memory budgets.

item.title: PACT bridges improve benchmarks, but gains can come without sender information
item.description: PLatour connects frozen models with trainable linear bridges, but controlled tests found some gains could be reproduced with uninformative signals or receiver-only training. That caveat matters when evaluating whether cross-model transfer actually uses the larger model’s information.

item.title: Multi-layer Indexer overlaps sparse-attention selection with attention compute
item.description: Adjacent layers often select similar tokens, so MLI reuses the previous layer’s selection and runs indexer scans concurrently with attention. It works in SGLang’s production decode graph without new weights or kernel changes, offering a practical way to hide long-context indexing overhead.

item.title: HyperFlow H3 Flash cuts a 31B video-audio model to 14B and six sampling steps
item.description: The compressed model generates synchronized video and stereo audio in six steps; the excerpt reports 36 seconds for a 5.2-second clip on one H200. These size and latency figures help assess the hardware cost of multimodal generation.

item.title: Muir allocates attention gates by sensitivity and reweights state readout
item.description: Muir uses lower-rank erase gates and matched-filter readout for linear attention, and addresses numerical instability in chunkwise algorithms at large chunk sizes. The mechanisms and implementation concerns are relevant to engineers building efficient long-context models.

item.title: LiveFoley streams video-to-audio with sliding windows and variable hops
item.description: LiveFoley uses a trailing sliding window to stream visual features without retraining and a variable-hop framework to trade latency against computation, alongside a widened diffusion denoising window. These techniques address latency and quality constraints in real-time generative inference, though the excerpt gives no measured results.

item.title: KVCache Meetup Korea covered CXL, GPU memory bottlenecks and serving software
item.description: Talks covered CXL memory expansion, GPU and HBM bottlenecks, request scheduling on RNGD and LMCache MP Mode. These are practical directions for managing KV-cache capacity and inference serving.

item.title: Reshard collective speeds RL weight refit by up to 5.7×
item.description: Reshard transfers only the required shard intersections between training and inference layouts, avoiding redundant gather-and-broadcast traffic; NeMo RL benchmarks show 2.7×–5.7× speedups. Faster refits can reduce a significant communication cost in large-model post-training.

item.title: TensorRT LLM speeds FLUX 3 image generation up to 1.62x on B200
item.description: The post reports up to 1.62× faster text-to-image generation with NVFP4, fused GEMM kernels, and torch.compile, plus separate gains from sparse attention and step caching. The measurements show practical inference trade-offs between latency and image fidelity.

item.title: SageMaker Inference adds GPU partitioning with NVIDIA MIG
item.description: SageMaker can now divide a physical GPU into isolated partitions with dedicated compute and memory, allowing multiple models to share an accelerator. This gives inference teams more flexibility to match deployments to model resource needs.

item.title: Speculative Listening drafts speech-model outputs before the next audio chunk arrives
item.description: The training-free method drafts output during idle listening time and verifies it when audio arrives; the authors report that incoming audio leaves 95.3% of chunk outputs unchanged. It offers a lossless way to use otherwise idle compute in chunked speech generation.

item.title: Google Cloud Z4M offers up to 168,000 GiB SSD and 400 Gbps RDMA
item.description: Z4M instances target AI training, inference, distributed KV caches and parallel file systems, with up to 168,000 GiB of local SSD and 400 Gbps RDMA. The stated storage and network limits matter when sizing infrastructure to keep accelerators supplied with data.

item.title: D3D enables asynchronous speculative decoding with up to 7.48× speedup
item.description: D3D drafts successor token blocks during target-model verification; it reports average speedups of 5.00× and 5.71× with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B, and 7.48× on GSM8K with Qwen3-32B. The standalone drafter and public code make this a practical inference optimization to examine.

item.title: LoopVQ compresses looped-transformer KV caches to 0.5 bits per element
item.description: LoopVQ jointly vector-quantizes channels across loop steps and fine-tunes codebooks; at 0.5 bits per element, it outperforms existing KV-cache quantizers on reasoning and retrieval tasks. The approach targets a memory bottleneck in parameter-efficient looped models.

item.title: SIMPLE predicts LLM inference energy without per-model calibration
item.description: SIMPLE separates prefill and decode energy into four parameters and reports R² of 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE across 13 dense LLMs on H100 GPUs, outperforming the cited baseline by 3.1–3.5×. Its architectural model can help teams estimate inference energy and understand KV-cache costs.

item.title: NVIDIA's serving stack treats KV cache as a fleet-wide resource
item.description: The design combines KV-aware routing and disaggregated serving with tiers spanning GPU, CPU, and storage; the excerpt also says NVFP4 reduces model footprint by about 3.5× versus FP16. These are practical levers for trading memory capacity against serving concurrency.

item.title: Linux power firmware limits RTX Spark inference to 14 tokens per second
item.description: On Linux, the laptop’s GPU reportedly drops to about 780 MHz on wall power, cutting a 120B-model run from roughly 65 tokens per second to under 14; a Windows-only power-management component is identified as the cause. The findings show how firmware and OS support can dominate local inference performance.

item.title: Cryptographic proofs could verify which model produced an inference
item.description: The report argues that proofs can bind a provider to a model and verify that each response came from it, guarding against substitution or token-stream tampering. This could make model identity auditable in applications where routing and security matter.

item.title: SpecOPD parallelizes on-policy training for speculative decoding drafters
item.description: SpecOPD trains speculative-decoding drafters from parallel branches, packing them into proposal trees to share target-prefix computation while preserving attention histories. The method targets the sequential rollout bottleneck in improving draft acceptance, though the excerpt reports no measured gains.

item.title: SpecPilot uses autonomous search to optimize speculative decoding per deployment
item.description: SpecPilot uses a cost model to identify gaps in speculative-decoding systems, then has parallel agents test and integrate optimizations; token forcing checks outputs against the stock system. The deployment-specific approach reflects the trade-offs involved in tuning inference systems.

item.title: Cartesia uses state-space models and AWS infrastructure for sub-100ms voice AI
item.description: The post says Cartesia uses purpose-built state-space models and AWS infrastructure for text-to-speech and speech-to-text under 100 milliseconds at global scale. The latency target and serving approach matter for engineers building real-time voice systems.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock adds India-based inference for Kimi K3
item.description: Bedrock now offers in-country Kimi K3 inference in India for data-residency needs; one customer reports 80% lower costs with prompt caching and 85% faster multi-turn chats. The release illustrates how regional serving and caching can affect production AI workloads.

item.title: Wave Forcing pipelines video denoising and cache refresh across replicas
item.description: Wave Forcing staggers denoising and cache-refresh stages across model replicas to produce one output chunk per concurrent forward round after pipeline fill. Its co-design of generation and runtime addresses throughput and quality challenges in streaming video inference.

item.title: Engineers compare hardware for running local LLMs
item.description: The discussion includes a used workstation with two V100 GPUs running Qwen3.8-27B Q4 at about 55 tokens per second, alongside other local-model setups. These firsthand configurations offer practical reference points for local inference hardware.

item.title: AB-Attention estimates dense video attention with sampled key-value blocks
item.description: This training-free method selects blocks with query clustering and inverse-inclusion-probability weighting to approximate dense attention at high sparsity. It targets the quadratic attention cost that dominates video diffusion inference.

item.title: A 510-byte boot-sector model generates Linux boot messages
item.description: A char-level neural network runs from a 510-byte MBR, with its weights and vocabulary in following sectors; its assembly inference matches a Python simulator character for character. It is a compact, concrete example of inference under extreme size constraints.

item.title: Quantized model files can be intact yet fail code-generation tests
item.description: An audit tested 305 official Ollama GGUF tags and 22 community files; importance-matrix quantization raised three Qwen2.5-Coder-3B builds from zero to 76–113 HumanEval+ tasks. The released audit data and quantcheck tool help teams validate local model artifacts before deployment.

item.title: Bedrock cost grows with agent autonomy and the context each task carries
item.description: Agent workflows make multiple model calls per task and carry larger contexts, so token spend depends on autonomy and context size, not just user interactions. Platform teams can use this framing to connect workload design with budgets and cost attribution.
